ing: for the dough, plus more to serve
st: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until very tender, then drain well and mash until smooth.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] of the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for 8 minutes until golden.
Mix the mashed potatoes, the onion, the farmer cheese, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper into a smooth filling. Let it cool.
In a large bowl mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt, the egg, the sour cream and the warm water. Knead for 5 minutes into a soft, smooth dough.
Cover the dough with a bowl and rest it for 30 minutes so it is easy to roll.
Roll the dough out thinly on a floured counter and cut rounds with a 3-inch cutter or a glass.
Put a heaping spoonful of filling in the middle of each round, fold it over, and pinch the edges tightly shut so no filling can leak.
Boil the pierogi in batches in a large pot of salted water. When they float, cook them 3 more minutes, then lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Melt the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter in a skillet and fry the boiled pierogi 2 minutes per side until lightly golden.
Serve hot with extra sour cream and any leftover fried onion.
Cook the bacon in a large heavy pot over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes more until soft.
Add the pork cubes and brown them on all sides, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes until they release their liquid.
Add the sauerkraut, the fresh cabbage, the tomato paste, bay leaves, allspice, pepper and salt, then pour in [[3 cups]] water and the wine.
Bring to a boil, cover, and lower the heat. Simmer for 1 hour, stirring now and then.
Add the sliced sausage and the prunes. Cover and simmer for 45 more minutes until the pork is very tender.
Taste and add salt or a splash of water if it looks dry. Bigos is even better reheated the next day.
Remove the bay leaves and serve hot with rye bread.
Hard-boil the eggs: lower them into boiling water for 10 minutes, then cool in cold water and peel.
Put [[6 cups]] water, the carrot, bay leaves, allspice and potatoes in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Add the sliced sausage and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are soft.
Stir in the sour rye starter and bring back to a gentle simmer for 10 minutes. Do not boil hard.
Add the garlic, marjoram, salt and pepper. Stir in the cream if using.
Taste and adjust: add more starter for more sourness, or more salt.
Ladle into bowls and add halved eggs. Serve with rye bread.
Put the broth, beets, carrots, onion, bay leaves and allspice in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, partly covered, for 40 minutes until the beets are tender.
Strain the soup through a sieve into a clean pot and discard the vegetables, or keep the beets to serve in the bowls.
Add the garlic, vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper. Warm gently for 5 minutes; do not boil or the red color fades.
Taste and adjust the sour and sweet balance with a little more vinegar or sugar.
Stir in the dill and serve hot in cups or with boiled potatoes.
Cut out the core of the cabbage. Boil the whole head in a large pot for 8 minutes, peeling off soft outer leaves with tongs as they loosen.
Cook the rice in water for 8 minutes until half done, then drain. Cook the onion in the butter for 5 minutes until soft.
Mix the pork, rice, onion, egg, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper by hand until just combined.
Trim the thick rib on each cabbage leaf. Place about [[3 tbsp]] filling near the base of each leaf, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Line a heavy pot with a few torn leaves and pack the rolls in, seam side down.
Mix the crushed tomatoes, broth, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and bay leaves, then pour over the rolls.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1 hour 15 minutes, or bake at 350°F (175°C), until the pork reaches 160°F (71°C).
Serve hot with the tomato sauce spooned over.
Put the potatoes in salted water, boil for 18 minutes until tender, drain, and toss with [[1 tbsp]] of the butter and the dill. Keep warm.
Place each pork chop between plastic wrap and pound with a heavy pan until about 1/4 inch thick.
Season both sides of the pork with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Set up three plates: flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs. Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing gently.
Heat the oil and the remaining [[3 tbsp]] butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry the cutlets 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and the pork reaches 145°F (63°C). Fry in two batches if needed.
Drain the cutlets on paper towels and serve with the potatoes and a pinch of salt.
Grate the potatoes and onion on the small holes of a box grater into a bowl.
Squeeze the mixture in a clean towel over the sink to remove as much liquid as you can.
Mix in the egg, flour, salt and pepper right away so the potatoes do not darken.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Spoon in about [[3 tbsp]] batter per pancake and flatten to 1/2 inch thick. Fry 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels. Add the remaining oil between batches as needed.
Serve right away with sour cream.
Hold the onion halves cut side down in a dry skillet over medium-high heat for 4 minutes until dark brown.
Put the chicken in a large stockpot and cover with [[12 cups]] cold water. Bring slowly to a boil and skim off the foam.
Add the onion, carrots, parsnips, celery root, leek, bay leaves, allspice and peppercorns.
Lower the heat so the pot barely bubbles, partly cover, and simmer for 2 hours. Do not boil hard or the broth turns cloudy.
Lift out the chicken and carrots. Strain the broth through a fine sieve and season with the salt.
Pull the chicken meat from the bones and slice the carrots into rounds.
Cook the noodles in a separate pot of salted water for 4 minutes and drain.
Put noodles, chicken and carrots in bowls, ladle in the hot broth and sprinkle with parsley.
Chill the pork cubes in the freezer for 20 minutes so they grind cleanly.
Grind the pork through a coarse plate, or pulse in small batches in a food processor until coarsely chopped.
Mix the pork with the garlic, marjoram, onion, pepper, salt and [[0.25 cup]] cold water by hand for 2 minutes until sticky.
Fry a small spoonful to taste and adjust salt and garlic.
Stuff the mix into casings with a stuffer and twist into 6-inch links. No casing? Shape into thick patties instead.
Place the links in a pot of water at 175°F (80°C), not boiling, and poach for 25 minutes until the center reaches 160°F (71°C).
Brown the poached links in the oil in a skillet for 6 minutes. Warm the sauerkraut alongside and serve together.

ing: cut in half lengthwise, each about 10 inches
st: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Cut each baguette in half lengthwise to make four long open halves.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes.
Add the mushrooms, salt and pepper and cook 8 minutes until all the liquid has evaporated and they are browned.
Toast the baguette halves cut side up on a baking sheet for 4 minutes.
Spoon the mushroom mixture over the bread and top with the shredded cheese.
Bake for 8 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and golden.
Drizzle with ketchup in zigzags, add chives and serve hot.
Stir the yeast and [[1 tbsp]] of the sugar into the warm milk and let stand for 10 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl whisk the egg yolks, egg, the remaining sugar, melted butter, vanilla and salt, then add the yeast milk.
Add [[4 cups]] flour and mix, then knead for 8 minutes until the dough is soft and springy.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Roll the dough 1/2 inch thick and cut 3-inch rounds. Place on a floured tray, cover, and let rise 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C). Check with a thermometer.
Fry 3 doughnuts at a time, 1.5 minutes per side, until deep golden with a pale band around the middle.
Drain on paper towels. Fill a piping bag with the jam and pipe [[1 tbsp]] into each doughnut through a small hole in the side.
Dust with the powdered sugar and eat the same day.
Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Mix the crushed cookies with the melted butter and press into the bottom of a 9-inch springform pan.
Beat the softened butter with [[0.5 cup]] sugar until pale and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Beat in the egg yolks one at a time, then mix in the farmer cheese, flour, vanilla and lemon zest until smooth.
In a clean bowl beat the egg whites with the salt until foamy, then add the remaining [[0.5 cup]] sugar and beat to stiff peaks.
Gently fold the whites into the cheese mixture in two parts without deflating them.
Pour into the pan and bake for 1 hour 10 minutes until set at the edge with a slight wobble in the center.
Turn off the oven, crack the door open, and let the cake cool inside for 1 hour to prevent cracking.
Chill in the fridge for at least 4 hours, then release the pan and slice.
Mix [[4 cup]] flour, [[2.25 tsp]] yeast, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[1.5 tsp]] salt. Add [[1.25 cup]] warm milk and [[2 tbsp]] butter.
Knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and rise 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 10 pieces. Roll each into a 14 inch rope and twist two thin ropes together, or twist a single rope, then join the ends into a ring.
Rest the rings 20 minutes. Meanwhile bring a wide pot of water to a gentle boil and heat the oven to 400°F.
Boil each ring for 1 minute per side, turning once. Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain.
Brush with beaten egg, press into [[0.25 cup]] sesame seeds, and bake 18 to 20 minutes until golden brown.
nt: Best swap: leave out the egg wash and brush with milk for a dairy-lighter, egg-free finish.

st: Stir the yeast and [[1 tbsp]] sugar into the warm milk and leave 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour, [[0.25 cup]] sugar, butter and egg with the yeast milk. Knead 8 minutes until smooth, cover and let rise 1 hour.
Simmer the poppy seeds with the honey, raisins, orange zest and [[0.5 cup]] water for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick. Cool.
Roll the dough into a 12 by 16 inch rectangle, spread the poppy filling over it leaving a 1 inch border, then roll up tightly from the long side.
Place seam side down on a lined baking tray, cover and rest 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 350°F.
Brush with the beaten yolk and bake for 40 minutes until deep golden. Cool fully before slicing.
nt: Best swap: use a 12 oz canned poppy seed filling in place of the homemade filling.

st: Mix the flour, egg, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 cup]] warm water. Knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest 20 minutes.
Cook the onion in the butter over medium heat for 5 minutes, add all mushrooms and cook 10 minutes until the liquid cooks off. Stir in the breadcrumbs, a little salt and pepper. Cool.
Simmer the beets, peeled and grated, in the broth with marjoram for 30 minutes. Strain and season to make a clear red borscht.
Roll the dough thin and cut 2 inch squares.
Put a half teaspoon of filling on each square. Fold into a triangle, pinch the edges and join the two ends around your finger to make little ears.
Boil the uszka in salted water for 4 minutes until they float, then drain.
Serve a handful in each bowl of hot borscht.
nt: Best swap: replace the dried porcini with extra button mushrooms and a splash of soy sauce for depth.
